correctness.rationale: A finite reduced ring is a product of finite fields. In that product, the principal ideal of a vertex is determined exactly by its nonempty proper coordinate support, so cozero adjacency is support incomparability and each support class has size \(\prod_{i\in A}(q_i-1)\). Distinct supports have distinct open neighborhoods, making these precisely the false-twin classes. Their quotient is the incomparability graph of the proper nonempty Boolean lattice and has \(2^r-2\) vertices, recovering \(r\). For \(r\ge3\), its minimum-degree vertices are exactly singleton and co-singleton supports, forming two \(K_r\) cliques joined by a perfect matching. One side’s twin-class sizes recover \(q_i-1\); swapping the sides can satisfy both matched multiplicity equations only when all factors are \(\mathbb F_2\), where no ambiguity remains. For \(r=2\), the graph is \(K_{q_1-1,q_2-1}\). The packaged exhaustive verifier was inspected, and the symbolic reconstruction independently checks the side-swap argument.
residual_risks: The theorem is explicitly within the finite reduced nonfield class; no claim is made against nonreduced graph twins.

originality.rationale: Earlier work develops the reduced cozero-divisor graph precisely by collapsing principal-ideal multiplicities and studies decomposition into fields/local rings; the available primary-text roadmap confirms that emphasis. Afkhami-Khashyarmanesh supply the two-field complete-bipartite structure, and later work focuses on genus, spectra and other graph parameters. The assigned reconstruction exploits information the reduced graph discards: false-twin multiplicities over Boolean supports. Targeted current searches found no theorem that the full cozero-divisor graph determines every finite reduced nonfield ring or recovers all field orders. The highly relevant 2010/2011 full PDFs could not be completely retrieved through the available lawful access paths, so this remains a stated literature risk rather than negative evidence.
residual_risks: The inaccessible complete 2010/2011 text is the main literature-access risk; inaccessible literature alone is not treated as an originality failure.
A theorem under principal-ideal multiplicity or graph blow-up terminology could be poorly indexed.

value.rationale: Graph reconstruction of the complete finite reduced ring within a natural ring class is a strong structural statement: the graph recovers not only the number of field factors but every field order. The false-twin/Boolean-quotient mechanism explains exactly which information the reduced graph loses and how the full graph restores it. This is a natural classification result, not a small numerical invariant.
residual_risks: The reduced and nonfield hypotheses are essential, so the theorem is not a classification of arbitrary finite rings from cozero-divisor graphs.
